round3_reverse.hypothesis_feedback: Round 3's reverse loop confirms round 3's forward finding by rebuilding the model from the OTHER direction: the 'reduced' model is numerically identical to the full model, because neither round-3 proposal (a mu_sym length bridge; dropping the PTA sector) was actually accepted as a tier A/B/L reduction (ledger.ladder round-3 entry, 'how': 'none'). This is verified STRUCTURALLY (reduced_model.frozen_lcdm_dark_energy() takes zero mu_sym/c4_pta_product arguments, confirmed by reading the code), not by a self-comparing probe -- an earlier draft of chi2_aic_bic.py claimed an 'independent refit agreement' from a check that in fact called the same cached frozen-LCDM function three times; corrected in place after advisor review, see chi2_aic_bic_report.json's cross_check_caveat and chi2_flat_verification_seed43.note. Independent re-sweep (fresh seed 43, not round 3 forward's seed 42) reproduces the forward round's TDA anomaly under a different seed: the PCA dimension of the model's observable cloud (pca_k=2) DOES match the task's own predictor ('dimension = number of remaining free params' = 2, a HIT), but the connected-component count (Betti b0=[2] observed vs [1] predicted) does not, at both seeds -- so the b0 mismatch is a property of the sparse-Rips complex at this cloud size/density, not seed noise, while the dimension prediction itself is correct. TDA bottleneck orderings also disagree by homology dimension (model closer to real than the null in H1, but the null is closer than the model in H0), reconfirming TDA's already-declared status here as a sanity gate, not evidence. The quantitative AIC/BIC numbers this loop direction adds (delta_AIC=+4.00, delta_BIC=+14.76 vs frozen Lean-pinned LCDM, for zero chi2 change) are DEFINITIONAL given the disclosed k-counting convention (2 untested parameters cost 2k in AIC, k*ln(N) in BIC by formula alone, not from any new measurement) -- they restate, rather than newly test, round 3's own chi2-flatness finding, quantified. In plain words: the theory does not yet need mu_sym or c4_pta_product to explain the data available -- dark energy IS (so far, indistinguishably) the frozen self-dual/Lean constant, and the remaining two knobs are invisible to every real dataset in hand, not derived away. What the theory must change, going forward, is not the sweep or the fit: it is either (a) find or fetch a real dataset that mu_sym or c4_pta_product actually move (a torsion-balance/fifth-force table for mu_sym via the 47-micron self-dual length already computed in round3/mu_sym_length_bridge_report.json, tier C and explicitly disfavored by a factor of a few per LeanMaster's own DarkEnergyScale.lean docstring; or a real angular Hellings-Downs/optimal-statistic NANOGrav product for c4_pta_product, currently ABSENT), or (b) formally drop both under S3's 'scope, not derivation' rule -- which needs a code change outside this audit-only worktree's permitted scope (workshopcosmo.py / param_loop_sim.py signatures) to convert from a bookkeeping label into an actual removal, the same code-change gate that has stalled lambda_sym's removal since round 2.
